newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Russians, Chechens establish consultative council.
newsitem.headline: Russians, Chechens establish consultative council.

text.p: High level delegations from Russia and Chechnya have agreed to form a consultative council to solve some of their many differences, the organiser of a peace-brokering conference said on Saturday.

"We have agreement on a joint statement... we didn't expect it.... We had a lot of discussions on practical measures...and the parties have agreed to establish an informal consultative council," William Ury, the conference chairman, told Reuters.

The joint statement reached recognises the need to foster understanding and cooperation and to provide economic assistance to the Chechen Republic, the latter being the focus of the planned consultative council.

The delegations, including Vyacheslav Mikhailov, Russia's Minister of Nationalities and Chechnya's Vice President Vakha Arsanov, met in the neutral surrounds of the Netherlands on Friday and Saturday.

The conference, supervised by U.S. based Conflict Management Group and Harvard University and with the presidents of the Russian republics of Tatarstan and Ingushetia as mediators, was almost scuppered on Tuesday when two Russian fighters forced Arsanov to abort his flight to the Netherlands, but an apology and all-clear from Moscow on Wednesday allowed the Chechen delegation to leave.
The meeting was intended as a follow-up to the peace deal signed between Chechen President Asian Maskhadov and Russian President Boris Yeltsin on May 12 which formally ended 21 months of fighting.
